scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Dumhal is a traditional dance of the Watal tribe in Jammu and Kashmir.
It is a historical practice where only the men of the tribe are 'privileged' to perform, indicating a long-standing social structure and gender-specific ritual role within the community.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Dumhal is performed on specific occasions.
It carries a ritual significance, centered around the planting of a banner, and is an exclusive cultural right of the Watal men.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance begins with a ritualistic movement to dig a banner into the ground.
Once the banner is set, the men dance in a circle around it.
The movement is described as ritualistic and performed in a chorus.
Watch for Banner Planting.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: A circular formation revolving around a central banner planted in the ground.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Drums are the primary instruments used to assist the music.
The dancers themselves provide the vocals, singing together in a chorus as they move.
Listen for the Drums.

The sound is dominated by the resonant thrum of drums and the synchronized voices of a male chorus. There is a lack of melodic instrumentation, focusing the listener on the rhythmic chanting and the percussive beat that times the dancers' steps.
